The P2P>ATM milestone is itself an outcome, but its media visibility plausibly reinforces trust in digital rails and modestly supports continued adoption.
Mobile money interoperability historically raises active usage by removing walled-garden friction, as seen after Tanzania's 2021 interoperability push.
Interoperability lowers the cost of holding a second mobile money account, a small enabling effect on account ownership breadth.
National real-time payment rails (cf. India's UPI) sharply accelerate P2P and merchant digital payment volumes once launched.
Ubiquitous real-time payment rails make holding an account materially more useful, an enabling effect on new account formation over a longer horizon.
NFIS-II coordinates NBE, operators, and donors toward the 70% 2025 target; effects diffuse through many channels and are hard to isolate empirically from any single event.
NFIS-II includes gender-inclusion targets (see REC_0033 parity target for 2030); direct causal attribution to the 14% current share is uncertain.
A 20-82% tariff hike directly raises the cost of mobile data/voice relative to income (worsening this lower_better indicator).
Price increases can dampen usage frequency among price-sensitive users, a headwind to M-Pesa's active-usage growth.

Mandating Fayda for banking formalizes and secures accounts (positive) but risks temporarily excluding adults not yet enrolled (negative) — net direction is genuinely ambiguous until enrollment nears saturation.
Adding a second enrollment channel (Safaricom, 7 regions) plausibly accelerates enrollment throughput beyond Ethio Telecom's channel alone.
Crossing a large round-number milestone (29.5M) generates media coverage that plausibly reinforces enrollment momentum (bandwagon/signaling effect).
